source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why should you correct a remembered preference that came from a role-play example?

options.text: The example may not represent your actual preference.
options.feedback: A system can mistake an imagined role for a fact about you. Inspecting and correcting that memory prevents later work from inheriting the mistaken preference.

options.text: A preference mentioned in role-play is evidence of a lasting personal choice.
options.feedback: An example can describe an imagined role rather than you. Its appearance in conversation does not establish a recurring personal preference.

options.text: The stored version should take priority because it came from an earlier message.
options.feedback: Earlier context can be misinterpreted. Inspecting and correcting the memory helps it represent your actual preference.

options.text: The remembered preference can be treated as a record of completed project work.
options.feedback: A preference guides recurring choices; project state tracks changing facts and operations. Neither role turns a fictional example into a fact about you.
